irrigation.title: Water advisor
irrigation.subtitle: How much to irrigate in the next few days
irrigation.estimateNotice: These are calculated estimates (FAO-56 method with weather forecast), not sensor readings. Check soil moisture by hand before irrigating.
irrigation.noForecast: Weather forecast is not available. Enter expected temperatures and rain below; the estimate will use your numbers.
irrigation.noLocation: No location is set, so there is no forecast. Enter expected temperatures and rain below, or set your location on the home screen.
irrigation.manualNote: The same values are used for every day. These are your inputs, not a forecast.
irrigation.rainCovered: Rain is expected to cover the crop's need on {n} day(s). Skip irrigation on those days.
irrigation.method_note: Assumes {eff}% irrigation efficiency for this method. 1 mm over 1 m² = 1 litre.
irrigation.latAssumed: Location coordinates unknown: latitude 11°N (Tamil Nadu average) assumed.

soil.light_frequent: This soil holds less water. Give smaller amounts more often rather than one heavy watering.
soil.heavy_less_often: This soil holds water well. Water less often and avoid waterlogging; check that cracks have not opened before irrigating.
soil.medium: This soil holds water moderately. Irrigate when the top few centimetres feel dry.

warn.heavy_rain: Heavy rain (50 mm or more) is forecast. Postpone irrigation and keep drainage channels open.
warn.heat: Very hot days (38°C or more) are forecast. Irrigate in the early morning or evening to reduce losses.
warn.paddy_flooded: Paddy is usually grown with standing water; this estimate covers crop water use only, not ponding or percolation losses.
warn.crop_finished: By this date the crop has passed its usual duration. Irrigation is normally stopped before harvest.

err.days: Sowing date must be today or earlier (within 400 days)
err.area: Area must be between 0 and 1000 acres
err.temp: Enter valid temperatures (max must be at least min)
err.rain: Rain must be between 0 and 500 mm

irrigation.how: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) is estimated with the Hargreaves equation (FAO-56, eq. 52) from daily max/min temperature and your latitude. Crop water use = ET₀ × crop coefficient (Kc, FAO-56 Table 12) for the current growth stage. Rain below 5 mm is ignored and 80% of larger rain is counted as effective. The remaining need is divided by the method's efficiency to get the water to apply.
